newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan urges China to reopen talks on anniversary.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan urges China to reopen talks on anniversary.

text.p: Taiwan urged China on Tuesday to renew semi-official talks across the Taiwan strait, saying Hong Kong's July 1 handover to Beijing may open a new opportunity for the rivals to mend ties.

"Frank communications, without any kind of precondition, between both sides will open the door," Straits Exchange Foundation chairman Koo Chen-fu said in a statement marking the fourth anniversary of groundbreaking talks between Taipei and Beijing.

Taiwan and China, split since a civil war ended in 1949, met in Singapore on April 29, 1993, through the quasi-official foundation and its mainland counterpart, the Association for Relations Across the Taiwan Strait.
A series of technical meetings on civilian issues followed but talks have been suspended since mid-1995 after Taiwan President Lee Teng-hui paid a private but high-profile visit to the United States.
China, which has viewed Taiwan as a renegade province, said Lee's visit was an attempt to promote independence for Taiwan rather than reunification with the mainland.
Koo said the British colony's return to Chinese rule on July 1 offered an opportunity to break the ice.
"Hong Kong's return to China on July 1 is the end of colonial rule of west European powers. We should view it positively," Koo said.
"We also hope this will be the turning point to rebuild mutual trust across the Taiwan strait," he said without elaboration.
Taiwan and China should work together to ensure Hong Kong's prosperity and growth, Koo said.
In a sign of possibly improved relations, the Taipei foundation's deputy secretary-general, Lee Ching-ping, left for China on Monday.
Lee and his private delegation were scheduled to meet mainland officials to discuss problems over a previous agreement on cross-strait document authentication.
Taiwan still bans all direct official contacts with the mainland, notwithstanding a thaw in the 1980s that allowed semi-official talks to take place.
Taiwan has repeatedly urged China to resume semi-official talks to resolve issues facing both sides -- including fishing disputes, repatriation of airline hijackers and stowaways.
